title: Coefficient Ideal Equals the gcd Ideal
content: The lemma span_range_eq_span_gcd is the technical heart of the file: it identifies the ideal generated by the coefficients a : Fin n → ℤ with the principal ideal generated by their Finset gcd. The proof is a double inclusion. For span (Set.range a) ⊆ span {gcd}: each coefficient aᵢ is a multiple of the gcd (Finset.gcd_dvd), so it lies in span {gcd}, and Ideal.span_le lifts this to the whole span. For the reverse span {gcd} ⊆ span (Set.range a): because ℤ is a principal ideal ring, the coefficient ideal has a generator g; since each aᵢ lies in span {g}, g divides every aᵢ, hence g divides the gcd by the universal property Finset.dvd_gcd, placing the gcd inside span {g} = span (Set.range a). Identifying these two ideals is what lets the existential gcd of the parent file be replaced by the concrete, computable Finset gcd.
mathContext: Over a PID, an ideal is determined by the divisibility data of its generators. The family ideal $\langle a_1, \dots, a_n\rangle$ and the principal ideal $\langle \gcd(a_1,\dots,a_n)\rangle$ have the same divisors, hence are equal. Concretely $\gcd(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ is a $\mathbb{Z}$-linear combination of the $a_i$ (multivariable Bézout), witnessed here abstractly through the principal generator.
prerequisites: greatest common divisor in a GCD monoid

title: Explicit gcd Form of n-variable Bézout
content: solvable_iff_gcd_dvd states that Σ aᵢxᵢ = b has an integer solution iff (Finset.univ.gcd a) ∣ b. The proof first rewrites solvability as ideal membership: by Ideal.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun, a solution x with Σ aᵢxᵢ = b is exactly a certificate that b ∈ span (Set.range a) (the mul_comm massages aᵢ·xᵢ versus xᵢ•aᵢ). Then span_range_eq_span_gcd rewrites the coefficient ideal as the principal ideal of the gcd, and Ideal.mem_span_singleton turns membership into divisibility. The upgrade over the parent file's linear_bezout_n is that the witness d is no longer an existentially quantified object characterized by abstract gcd axioms — it is the single, computable value Finset.univ.gcd a.
mathContext: Multivariable Bézout: the linear Diophantine equation $\sum_{i} a_i x_i = b$ is solvable over $\mathbb{Z}$ iff $\gcd(a_1, \dots, a_n) \mid b$. Equivalently, $b$ lies in the lattice (ideal) generated by the coefficients. This is the degree-1, single-equation base case of the Smith-normal-form solvability theory for integer linear systems.
prerequisites: the parent file's existential Bézout characterization

title: Linear Forms and the Decidability Criterion
content: The LinearForm n structure bundles coefficients (Fin n → ℤ) with a constant term, and LinearForm.Solvable asks for an integer assignment making Σ coeffsᵢ·xᵢ + const vanish. LinearForm.solvable_iff reduces this to (Finset.univ.gcd coeffs) ∣ const. The proof shifts the constant to the right-hand side — Σ coeffsᵢ·xᵢ + const = 0 is equivalent to Σ coeffsᵢ·xᵢ = -const (linarith in both directions) — then applies solvable_iff_gcd_dvd and dvd_neg (a ∣ -c ↔ a ∣ c). This is the form needed for a decision procedure, since both the gcd and the divisibility test are effective over ℤ.
mathContext: A linear form $\sum_i c_i x_i + c$ vanishes for some integer point iff $\gcd(c_1,\dots,c_n) \mid c$. The sign flip on the constant is immaterial because $a \mid -c \iff a \mid c$.

title: Decidable Instance and Degree-1 Hilbert's Tenth Problem
content: Because integer divisibility is decidable and Finset.gcd is computable, decidable_of_iff' transports decidability across LinearForm.solvable_iff to give the instance LinearForm.decidableSolvable. The capstone linear_h10_decidable then states DecidablePred (LinearForm.Solvable) for every n: solvability of linear Diophantine equations is decidable uniformly in the number of variables. This is the decidable lower edge of the Hilbert's-Tenth-Problem complexity hierarchy — in deliberate contrast to the parent file, where degree-4 equations in 9 variables (Jones 1982) are undecidable. The entire development is axiom-free, unlike the parent, whose MRDP/Jones results are axiomatized.
mathContext: Degree-1 H10 is decidable for all $n$: a single $\gcd$ computation and one divisibility check decide $\sum_i a_i x_i = b$. The undecidable frontier is degree 4 in 9 variables; the decidable frontier proved here is degree 1 in any number of variables. The gap (degrees 2–3, variable counts 3–8) remains open.
